subs: Saved across 3 floppy disks. Disk 2 is missing.
The intro was longer than the website.
Read aloud, the homepage said: “image, image, image.”
It fit on the phone. You needed tweezers to tap it.
One hand. Moving bus. Tiny button. Design for that.
Approved by the design system committee. Next meeting: Q3.
Thin grey text on white. Elegant. Unreadable.
The client is in the file now.
Then we invited the people we were designing for.
Two worked for everyone. The designer knew which two.
The requests kept changing. The job kept growing.
Captions were made for deaf and hard-of-hearing viewers. You just read a whole video of them.
spoken: [The client] Can you make the logo bigger?
[The client, by fax] Can you make the logo bigger?
[The client, by email] Can we add an intro?
[A visitor using a screen reader] What does this page say?
[The client] Does it work on my phone?
[Someone on a bus, one hand free] I can’t hit the button.
[The client] Can it look the same everywhere?
[Someone with low vision] I can’t read the grey text.
[The client] Can I get edit access?
[People invited to test it] We left some notes.
[The client] Can’t AI just do this?
[Automated accessibility check] Low contrast: 40. Alt text says “image”: 26. Pass: 2.
[The client] Love it. Can you make the logo bigger?
